summary: The scan now keeps which phase of a folder's read failed. DirectoryReader.Opened is set when Read's open returns a handle (the plain fallback counts), and Scanner.FailedKind(error, opened, listed) stamps UnreadableKind once in FolderDone: entries kept give ListedPartway, an open without entries gives the new OpenedNothingListed (appended as value 2), and anything else gives NothingListed. The tracker row (TopLevelRow.FailedKind replaces ListedPartway) and the tree (FolderTreeSession now takes result.Unreadable) read that stamp, and all three surfaces word it through UnreadableRows.KindText. The acceptance test passes, the Core suite is 964/964, and the published exe on the real fsa-guard-tests folder shows all 27 code-363 rows still NothingListed. Of the 7 files already modified when I began, I kept the engine-appended settled rules in .taad/fitness.yaml and the repro bug-test project unchanged.

obligations.how: C-001: UnreadableFolderTests.AFolderThatOpenedAndFailedItsFirstPageIsOpenedNothingListedBesideARefusedOne scans a deny-ListDirectory folder (error 5, opened=false) and asserts NothingListed, 'could not be opened' in the list and 'a-refused  (could not be opened)' on the top-level row; the bug test's control half asserts the same.

C-002: the SL-106 bug test (acceptance command) passes: b-opened, first page forced to 59 through OverrideQueryError, is recorded OpenedNothingListed with ChildCount 0 and neither the list nor the top-level title says 'could not be opened'. The Core.Tests Fact beside it asserts the exact words on both.

C-003: UnreadableFolderTests.AFolderOpenedByTheFallbackAfterItsKeepOpenWasRefusedIsOpenedNothingListedWhenItsFirstPageFails denies WriteAttributes on one folder; its dry run asserts the scan asked to keep and was refused for exactly that folder (LastAccessAsked-LastAccessKept == 1) and that it listed in full, then injects 59 and expects OpenedNothingListed. Shown red when Opened is taken from the keep-last-access attempt.

C-004: TopLevelRowTextTests.AFolderListedPartwayIsNotReadInFullAndOneNeverOpenedIsNotOpened (995 at the third buffer) expects ListedPartway, 'b-big  (only partly read)', and for c-top a failure below the row's own folder: Done, UnreadableBelow 2, FailedKind null. CancelledFolderTests still pins the record as ListedPartway.

C-005: ScannerFailedKindTests.AnUnaskedFirstPage995IsOpenedNothingListedAndACancelledOneLeavesNoRecord injects 995 on a first page with no cancel (OpenedNothingListed, title 'opened, but nothing could be listed') and cancels during that same call (status Cancelled, Unreadable empty). The Theory also pins 995 with listed>0 as ListedPartway.

C-006: ScannerFailedKindTests.TheKindFollowsThePhaseTheReaderSawAndNeverTheCode has rows for 5, 32, 363 and 1920 with opened=false giving NothingListed, and 5 with opened=true giving OpenedNothingListed. HeldFolderReasonTests (real sharing violation 32) passes unchanged, and the real 27 code-363 rows stay NothingListed in the W-001 run on the published exe.

C-007: ContainerLayerStoreTests.TheReaderRefusesAndCountsAFolderUnderTheStoreWithNoOpen now asserts Opened is false with Read returning -1 (and true for the folder beside the store). StoreSkipped passes failed: null; TheStoreAsATopLevelRowIsNotScannedNeitherDoneNorUnreadable still asserts NotScanned with an empty Unreadable.

C-008: UnreadableRowsTests.EveryKindHasWordsOfItsOwnAndOnlyARefusedOpenSaysItCouldNotBeOpened enumerates Enum.GetValues<UnreadableKind>(): distinct words, none the fallback, only NothingListed says 'could not be opened'; (UnreadableKind)99 and null give 'could not be read' without throwing.

C-009: FolderTreeSessionTests (FolderTreeSession.cs linked into Core.Tests): entry in the record, entry not in it, an entry held twice keeps its first kind, a closed session and FolderTreeSession.None give null, and a session over a real scan gives each failed folder its stamped kind.

C-010: WindowCases.ps1 -Case T-007 passes against the published exe with the expectation changed to 'only partly read': P reads that with an expander and 355 children, and R reads 'could not be opened' through the session lookup with no expander. The full WindowCases -Case All passed too (N-* not run).

C-012: W001OracleCorpus.json row F16 (OpenedNothingListed, code 5, plant listable, expect opened-nothing-listed); Get-OracleRow returns that class before the code-5 open; W001OracleTests.TheOracleGivesEveryRowOfTheCorpusItsClass passes in the 964-test suite.

C-013: TheAppNeverDecidesAFailedFolderKind and its fitness.yaml twin now use (?<!\?)\?\s*UnreadableKind\.\w+\b; plants.json F52 is a must-fire row for a ternary choosing OpenedNothingListed. The pattern was checked by regex only, since the harness was not run for F52. Parity prints AGREE 18 facts <- 22 twinned entries, 48 patterns (unchanged), RuleCases C-001 and C-003 hold, and both engine-appended settled rules match only their exempt files (Scanner.cs, UnreadableRows.cs).

DoneRowFinalityTests.MadeRow sets FailedKind=NothingListed through reflection for an Unreadable row; the SL-063 project passes 10/10 and was grepped (tests/bugs holds no other TopLevelRow construction that sets a state of Unreadable). I applied the mutation by hand: TheMarkShowsOnlyOnADoneRow went red with 'could not be read' vs 'could not be opened', then restored.

TitleOf's Unreadable arm is unconditional and words through KindText(UnreadableKind?), where null and unnamed values give 'could not be read'. TopLevelRowTextTests.AnUnreadableRowIsWordedFromItsKindAndNeverAsItsBareName pins the three kinds, null and 99.

Ran serially: WindowMutants.ps1 -Mutant All (all 12 passed), WindowCases.ps1 -Case T-003 (passed, open 1.5-1.9 ms warm) and -Case T-007, WindowCases -Case All, and the Core suite with --filter Network=TEST-NET-1. The last has 2 failures, CancellationTests.CancelReturnsFromAScanBlockedOnAnUnreachableShare and ...SameUnreachableShareScannedTwice (CancelsDelivered 0); both fail identically on HEAD c6d43e0 in an extracted copy, so they are not this slice's. obligations.how: The fallback Fact's dry run asserts LastAccessAsked >= 2 and LastAccessAsked - LastAccessKept == 1 (this folder alone refused), that the folder listed in full, and again after injection that it was refused. I applied the wrong placement by hand (Opened = keepLastAccess ? io.KeptLastAccess : true) and the Fact went red (NothingListed), then restored.

docs/design/SL-106-opened-then-failed.md has a 'Prior art, corrected' section that restates fts as a counter-example (gnulib's fts sets FTS_DNR from 'no items read', the conflation this slice removes) and says the design rests on the spikes. The fts authors are not named as support anywhere in the committed record.

deviations: KindText takes UnreadableKind? and TitleOf's Unreadable arm is unconditional (accepted finding m1), not the `when row.FailedKind is { }` arm the design wrote; a null kind reads 'could not be read' instead of falling to the bare name.
The design's Note rule is kept, but Note no longer re-reads the Unreadable flag for wording: an entry the record does not hold reads empty.

Added a direct DirectoryReader.Opened Fact (TheReaderSaysWhetherItsLastReadGotAHandle) and Opened assertions in ContainerLayerStoreTests, beyond the design's list, to pin the bit the whole stamp rests on.

The test helper FirstPageFailure hands the Created seam only to guards made on the calling thread, because the seam is a process-wide static and other test classes run in parallel; the repro test does not do this, and was left alone.
The settled rules (m4) got no plant rows and rule 2's delimiters were not widened: that finding is waived to SC-337 (O-019), so only the twinned rule's plant F52 was added.

The existing test name AFolderListedPartwayIsNotReadInFullAndOneNeverOpenedIsNotOpened keeps its old wording; its assertions are updated. Renaming it would change a name the design's case commands refer to.
